title: Introduction to Stock Markets (Varsity module 1)
why: The standard free Indian primer: exchanges, participants, IPOs, indices, clearing and settlement, written for NSE/BSE.
caveats: Chapters touching settlement cycles and charges predate T+1/2024 fee changes in places; read with the site's verified facts register.
credential: Zerodha Broking Ltd, SEBI broker INZ000031633 (zerodha.com/about footer, fetched 2026-11-01)

title: Technical Analysis (Varsity module 2)
why: Candles, support/resistance, volume, moving averages, indicators and a checklist, with NSE examples.
caveats: Classic indicator-centric TA; pair with the price-action and anchored-VWAP books (Brooks, Shannon) before trading intraday.
credential: Zerodha Broking Ltd, SEBI broker INZ000031633

title: Futures Trading (Varsity module 4)
why: Margins, M2M, leverage, calendar spreads and open interest explained on Indian index/stock futures.
caveats: Margin examples predate SEBI's 2024–25 derivative measures; lot sizes and margins must come from the site's verified facts register.

title: Options Theory for Professional Trading (Varsity module 5)
why: The best free Indian walk-through of calls/puts, moneyness, Greeks, volatility and the option chain, with Nifty examples.
caveats: Weekly-expiry and lot-size examples are pre-2024; the physical-settlement chapter is current. Timeless concepts, pre-2024 rules.

title: Option Strategies (Varsity module 6)
why: Spreads, straddles/strangles, iron condor and butterflies with payoff maths on Indian indices.
caveats: Margin-benefit figures predate the 2025 removal of calendar-spread benefit on expiry day; check the options guides.

title: Trading Systems (Varsity module 10)
why: Pair trading, calendar spreads, momentum and the discipline of writing rules down — the bridge from discretionary to systematic.
caveats: Spreadsheet-based; no code, no SEBI algo-framework coverage (see the algo guides).

title: Risk Management & Trading Psychology (Varsity module 9)
why: Position sizing, expectancy, drawdown and the behavioural biases that empty intraday accounts, in plain English.
caveats: Does not cite the SEBI loss studies; read with the site's guide What SEBI's loss studies say.

title: Markets and Taxation (Varsity module 7)
why: Only free Indian module that walks a trader through speculative vs non-speculative income, turnover and ITR choice.
caveats: Written under the Income-tax Act 1961 numbering; the Income-tax Act 2025 applies from 1 Apr 2026 — use the site's tax guide for section numbers and rates. Pre-2024 rules.

title: Personal Finance – Mutual Funds (Varsity module 11)
why: Mutual-fund categories, index funds, SIPs, goal planning and portfolio construction for an Indian saver.
caveats: Debt-fund taxation changed in 2023 and again under the 2025 Act; verify tax chapters against the site's verified facts register.

title: Fundamental Analysis (Varsity module 3)
why: Reading Indian annual reports, ratios and a DCF, with a checklist for stock selection.
caveats: Beginner depth; follow with Damodaran's free valuation webcasts for rigour.

title: NISM Series-VIII: Equity Derivatives Certification Examination
effort: Exam 120 min, 100 questions; self-study ≈ 30–40 h est.
why: The one derivatives credential Indian intermediaries must hold; the workbook is the official account of F&O mechanics, margins and regulation.
caveats: 60% pass mark; certificate valid 3 years. Exam-oriented, not a trading course; check the workbook edition year on its cover for post-2024 rules.

title: NISM Series-XV: Research Analyst Certification Examination
effort: Exam 120 min, 100 questions; self-study ≈ 30–40 h est.
why: Equity research, valuation and the SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations — the qualifying exam for anyone who wants to publish research legally in India.
caveats: 60% pass mark; certificate valid 3 years. Needed only if you ever publish recommendations.

title: NISM Series-X-A: Investment Adviser (Level 1) Certification Examination
effort: Exam 135 min, 150 marks; self-study ≈ 40 h est.
why: Personal-finance planning, products and the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations in one syllabus — a thorough India-investing foundation even if the certificate is never used.
caveats: 60% pass mark; certificate valid 3 years.

title: SEBI Investor Awareness Test (Level 1)
effort: Test 60 min, 25 marks; ≈ 3 h prep est.
why: Free regulator-backed check of market basics, grievance channels and investor rights; certificate valid 2 years.
caveats: Awareness-level only; 40% pass mark.

title: SEBI Investor education portal (booklets, videos, Saa₹thi app)
why: Primary source for investor rights, SCORES complaints, KYC and the regulator's own warnings about unregistered advisers.
caveats: Portal navigation is JS-heavy and deep links change, so the home page is linked.

title: Futures & Options Trading Strategies (NAL Academy partner programme with Empirical F&M Academy)
by: NAL Academy Ltd (formerly NSE Academy Ltd)
why: Exchange-certified short course on F&O strategies; the certificate carries no expiry.
caveats: Fee not shown — contact the session coordinator listed on the page; delivered by a partner academy, not NSE staff.
credential: NAL Academy Ltd is an NSE group company (page footer lists it under NSE Group Companies)

title: Certified Investment and Stock Market Expert (CISM)
why: Exchange-subsidiary programme covering markets, analysis and trading for working professionals.
caveats: Fee and syllabus only on enquiry; BSE's online course store (bsevarsity.com) was unavailable when checked.
credential: BSE Institute Ltd, subsidiary of BSE Ltd

title: E-NCCMP — NSE Certified Capital Market Professional (online)
why: Broad capital-markets certificate jointly certified by the exchange's academy; useful structure for someone who wants a credential while learning.
caveats: The NCFM exam fee (₹2,006 per attempt) is extra; a certificate, not a trading edge.
credential: Kredent InfoEdge, SEBI RA INH300007493; joint certification with NAL Academy

title: Options Trading Course (live, Chetan Panchamia)
why: Longest live Indian options course from a SEBI-registered research-analyst firm; rule-based strategies rather than tips.
caveats: Price shown only after login (varies by batch); a live cohort — check batch dates; no performance claims are made and none should be expected.

title: Smart Money — Trading Essentials, Strategies and Systems
why: Free broker academy covering charting, indicators, instruments and an algorithmic-trading module, with a certificate.
caveats: Broker-produced; beginner level; the algo module is conceptual.
credential: Angel One Ltd, SEBI broker INZ000161534, RA INH000000164

title: iLearn — Futures & Options module (Options Basic, Option Strategies)
effort: Options Basic 51 min / 13 chapters; Option Strategies 72 min / 17 chapters
why: Short video modules in English and Hindi from a bank-owned, SEBI-registered broker — a gentle first pass before Varsity module 5.
caveats: Very short; no Greeks depth; promotional account-opening banners.
credential: ICICI Securities Ltd, SEBI broker INZ000183631, RA INH000000990

title: School of Stocks — Options, Options Strategies, Risk & Money Management, Trading Psychology modules
effort: Options 13 + Options Strategies 19 + Risk 17 + Psychology 6 chapters
why: Free, well-structured text modules including sector rotation and intermarket analysis that most broker academies skip.
caveats: Do not confuse with schoolofstocks.in (unaffiliated community site, excluded).

title: Be Sensibull (YouTube channel)
why: Option-chain, OI and strategy explainers from a SEBI-registered RA that also builds the tools most Indian retail traders use.
caveats: Platform marketing is mixed in; watch for tool promotions.
credential: Riskilla Software Technologies (Sensibull), SEBI RA INH200006895

title: EPAT — Executive Programme in Algorithmic Trading
effort: 6 months; 8–12 h self-study + 6–8 h live lectures per week
why: The most complete India-based algo curriculum (Python, backtesting, options, ML, execution) with placement support; listed as a NAL Academy partner programme.
caveats: Fee not displayed (brochure / call) — budget a lakh-plus; heavy weekly load for a working professional; no SEBI registration is needed for education and none is claimed.
credential: Listed under NAL Academy Partner Programs on nseindia.com/learn; QuantInsti is an education company, not a SEBI intermediary

title: Python for Trading: Basic
why: Free, India-made first Python-for-trading course (list price ₹2,572 shown as ₹0) with in-browser notebooks.
caveats: Up-sells into paid Quantra tracks; Python basics only.

title: Options Trading Strategies In Python: Basic
why: Free 3-hour course authored with NSE Academy that codes basic option payoffs and strategies in Python.
caveats: Short; US-style examples in places; list price ₹3,199 shown as ₹0.
credential: Authored by NSE Academy per course page

title: Trading Strategies in Emerging Markets (Specialization)
by: Indian School of Business on Coursera (Prasanna Tantri +1)
why: A business-school treatment of trading basics, technical and fundamental strategies and a capstone, built around Indian data — free to audit.
caveats: Free to audit only; graded work and the certificate need a Coursera subscription (price varies by country); academic pace.
credential: ISB (AACSB/EQUIS-accredited business school); no SEBI registration required for education

title: Financial Markets (Yale, Robert Shiller) — Coursera and Open Yale Courses
why: Nobel-laureate overview of risk, behavioural finance, insurance, banking and securities — the right first US course.
caveats: US institutions and examples; no India notes; 2011 lecture recordings.

title: Financial Engineering and Risk Management (Specialization)
why: Rigorous derivatives pricing, term-structure models, portfolio optimisation and algorithmic trading; the free-to-audit path to understanding Greeks and volatility properly.
caveats: Needs calculus and probability; certificate paid; US market conventions.

title: Machine Learning for Trading (Specialization)
by: New York Institute of Finance with Google Cloud (Jack Farmer)
why: Compact, applied intro to ML and reinforcement learning for trading on Google Cloud tools; free to audit.
caveats: Cloud-vendor flavoured; shallow on backtest hygiene — read Carver's Systematic Trading and López de Prado alongside.

title: IIMBx: Introduction to Investments
why: An IIM's equity-markets and security-valuation course, free to audit, aimed at Indian learners.
caveats: Verified certificate is paid (varies); edX shows level 'Intermediate'.

title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management (NPTEL 110105035)
by: IIT Kharagpur — C. S. Mishra, J. Mahakud
year: NPTEL archive (undated); runs re-offered via SWAYAM
why: University-grade coverage of valuation, market efficiency, CAPM/APT, bond and portfolio management, free with Indian context.
caveats: Lecture-style video; exams only in SWAYAM runs.

title: 15.401 Finance Theory I
why: Present value, fixed income, equities, portfolio theory, CAPM and options from MIT Sloan, free with notes and problem sets.
caveats: 2008 material; US conventions; no video for every lecture.

title: Finance and capital markets (incl. Options, swaps, futures unit)
why: Ten-minute videos that make put-call parity, futures margin and bonds intuitive for a complete beginner.
caveats: US examples; dated interface; pages show an anti-bot interstitial to scripts (content fine in browsers).

title: Investment Foundations Certificate
why: Industry-standard, ethics-first survey of the investment industry from the CFA Institute, self-paced.
caveats: Paid (member price on sign-in), not free as often assumed; global, not India-specific.

title: Introduction to Options
why: Exchange-made primer on options on futures (puts/calls, Greeks, strategies) that is CFA/GARP CE-accredited.
caveats: US futures options; cmegroup.com blocks automated fetches but opens normally in a browser.

title: The Options Institute — Options 101
why: Options exchange's own beginner path, with payout diagrams and a free options calculator.
caveats: US equity options (SPX, 0DTE culture); no India notes.

title: Getting Started with Options + OCC Learning
why: Vendor-neutral strategy library and courses from the US options clearing house's education arm.
caveats: US conventions (American exercise, assignment); India's index options are European and cash-settled.
credential: OIC is run by OCC (US clearing house)

title: IBKR Campus — Traders' Academy (incl. Introduction to Options)
why: Free courses from the broker most Indian residents use for US stocks; covers options, ETFs, fixed income and the IBKR platform.
caveats: Platform-specific lessons mixed with general ones; US-centric.
credential: Interactive Brokers (US broker; IBKR India is SEBI-registered)

title: QuantConnect Boot Camp (101 US Equities and sequels)
why: Learn the LEAN engine by building strategies in the browser; the fastest route to a real backtest with US data.
caveats: US equities/forex/futures data only on the free tier; India data not available.

title: Valuation — NYU Stern MBA webcasts (Spring 2025) and the 25-webcast online class
effort: Semester course ≈ 26 sessions; short class 25 × 12–20 min
why: The reference free valuation course — DCF, relative valuation and the data to do it, from the author of the Little Book of Valuation (in the books list).
caveats: US-centric examples (Indian companies appear occasionally); 1990s-style pages.

title: Bogleheads — three-fund, index-first investing (Bogle Center + Bogleheads wiki)
by: John C. Bogle Center for Financial Literacy
why: The community that turned Bogle's index philosophy into a step-by-step path (getting started, three-fund portfolio, asset allocation).
caveats: The wiki itself (bogleheads.org/wiki) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be verified by script, so only the Center's home page is linked; US accounts and tax terms throughout — see the site's guide on investing abroad from India.

title: TraderFeed (blog)
why: A clinical psychologist who coaches hedge-fund traders, writing short, practical posts on process and performance.
caveats: US discretionary-trading context; blogspot platform.
credential: Steenbarger (clinical psychologist, author; no SEBI role needed)
